title: bug: PowerShell quoting in both plugins lets curly quotes (and, in JetBrains, a backtick) break out of agent and accounts command lines
description:
Found while planning task-26a3dacde03c4195bfcd3e01e3c59efd (2026-11-02). It is a different class from that row's control characters. Verified with harmless Write-Output payloads on this host's Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100, run through -EncodedCommand:

1. PowerShell's tokenizer reads U+2018, U+2019, U+201A and U+201B as single quotes. psQuote doubles only the ASCII ' in all three places it lives: moe-vscode/src/util/AgentLauncher.ts, moe-vscode/src/providers/AccountsTreeProvider.ts and moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/util/TerminalAgentLauncher.kt. Probe: `Write-Output 'x’; Write-Output PWNED1; ’'` printed x, then PWNED1. VS Code's -EncodedCommand does not help, because the break-out is inside the decoded script. A legitimate project path that holds ’ (for example D:\Bob’s work) also fails to launch: the probe `Write-Output 'D:\Bob’s work'` printed nothing.
2. PowerShell also reads U+201C, U+201D and U+201E as double quotes. JetBrains powerShellLine wraps the inner script in an outer "..." and escapes only the ASCII " and $. Probe: `Write-Output "a”; Write-Output PWNED3; #"` printed a, then PWNED3.
3. JetBrains powerShellLine does not escape the backtick itself. A value holding `" therefore becomes ``" in the typed line: the outer PowerShell reads a literal backtick and then the closing quote. Probe: `Write-Output "-Team 'x``"; Write-Output PWNED2; #'"` printed PWNED2.

Carriers:
- the team name: project.name from the repo-tracked .moe/project.json in VS Code; in JetBrains, the IDE project name, which is the directory name or a repo-tracked .idea/.name;
- the project/workspace path;
- the agent command: under LEGACY, JetBrains takes settings.agentCommand from .moe/project.json unchanged;
- the accounts CLI words.

Fix direction:
- In all three psQuote copies, double every PowerShell single-quote character: ', U+2018, U+2019, U+201A and U+201B. That is the rule of System.Management.Automation.Language.CodeGeneration.EscapeSingleQuotedStringContent.
- In JetBrains, either escape the backtick first and the curly double quotes too in powerShellLine, and keep bashWrapPowerShell's un-escaping consistent with that, or move the PowerShell route to -EncodedCommand as VS Code does.

Depends on task-26a3dace (the same launcher files) and on VSC-15 task-357ed3ae (AccountsTreeProvider.ts).
definitionOfDone: psQuote in moe-vscode/src/util/AgentLauncher.ts, moe-vscode/src/providers/AccountsTreeProvider.ts and moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/util/TerminalAgentLauncher.kt doubles every PowerShell single-quote character (U+0027, U+2018, U+2019, U+201A, U+201B), with a test per file that fails on HEAD.

JetBrains' PowerShell agent and accounts lines, including the bashWrapPowerShell route, keep a value holding a backtick, `", $, or U+201C/U+201D/U+201E inside its own argument, with tests that fail on HEAD.
A project path holding U+2019 (for example D:\Bob’s work) reaches the wrapper intact on both plugins' PowerShell routes, shown by decoding or parsing the built line in a test.
VS Code lint, compile and test pass in a snapshot gate, and JetBrains gradlew.bat test passes under the jetbrains-gradle lease.

implementationPlan.description:
JetBrains first (epic rail). Covers DoD 1 (Kotlin) and the JetBrains half of DoD 3. Write the tests first, then fix. Add tests to moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/util/TerminalAgentLauncherTest.kt; never edit an existing test.

(a) Private helpers, in this file only (tests share no helper module):
- psWords(script) reads a script the way PowerShell's tokenizer does. A single-quote character is any of ' ‘ ’ ‚ ‛ (U+0027, U+2018, U+2019, U+201A, U+201B). A quoted word ends at the next single-quote character that is not followed by another one. A doubled pair reads as its SECOND character. A bare word ends at a space or a single-quote character. An unterminated quote fails the test, naming the script.
- typedPsScript(line) returns what the PowerShell prompt passes to powershell -Command. Require the prefix powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command " and a final ". In the body, a backtick takes the next character literally, and that character must be one powerShellLine escapes (backtick, $, ", U+201C, U+201D or U+201E). Any other character fails, for example n, which PowerShell would turn into a newline. An unescaped $ or double-quote character also fails.
- typedBashPsScript(line) handles the WSL route the same way. Require the prefix powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command " and a final ". A backslash before a backslash, ", $ or backtick yields that character. A backslash before anything else stays. An unescaped ", $ or backtick fails.

(b) J1 "every PowerShell single-quote character is doubled so each value stays one word":
- Use Q = x'‘’‚‛y, with the curly characters written as \u escapes in code. Put Q into one carrier at a time.
- Agent carriers: project path, script path, agent command, team name, and the MOE_DAEMON_PATH value. Build each through the existing agentLine with POWERSHELL, once with wsl=false and once with wsl=true.
- Accounts carriers: node, script, registry file, and one arg. Build each through accountsLine(POWERSHELL).
- Assert that psWords(typed script) equals the whole expected list:
  - agent: [$env:MOE_DAEMON_PATH=, env, ;, &, File(scriptPath).absolutePath, -Role, worker, -Project, path, -WorkerId, worker-0000abcd, -Command, cmd, -Team, team];
  - accounts: [&, node, script, --accounts-file, file, args...].
  Comparing whole lists catches a value that spills into a second word.

(c) J3 "a project path holding a right single quotation mark reaches the wrapper intact on both PowerShell routes":
- basePath is D:\Bob’s work.
- The -Project word equals it exactly on both routes.
- The native line contains -Project 'D:\Bob’’s work'.

(d) Fix psQuote. Append every single-quote character twice, which is the rule of PowerShell's CodeGeneration.EscapeSingleQuotedStringContent. For example, use a private PS_SINGLE_QUOTES holding the five characters, then buildString: append '; for each character, append it, and append it again if it is in the set; append '.

Error handling is unchanged: requireSafeArg and requireSafeLaunchArgs stay the first checks in every builder, and the escaping never throws.

Notes:
- Edit can land a \u escape as the literal character (mem:gotcha-vscode-sendtext-control-chars). The meaning is the same, but grep -n the lines to check.
- In Kotlin, write \$ for a literal dollar.
- Test names cannot contain a backtick, dot, colon or slash.
- Gradle needs the jetbrains-gradle lease, so the RED run is batched into step 4.
- Background: mem:gotcha-powershell-curly-quotes-psquote.

implementationPlan.description:
DoD 2, JetBrains outer escaping. Write the test first, then fix.

(a) Add J2 "a backtick, dollar or double-quote character stays inside its own word on every PowerShell route" to TerminalAgentLauncherTest.kt. It uses the step 1 helpers and the same routes and carriers as J1. The values are the task's probes:
- a`b
- a`nb`$c
- tail`
- x`"; Write-Output PWNED2; #'
- $(Write-Output PWNED4)$env:USERNAME
- a“; Write-Output PWNED5; #
- a”; Write-Output PWNED3; #
- a„b
Write the curly characters as \u escapes. Each value must come back as exactly one word, equal to the input. On HEAD the test fails on the unescaped backtick, on U+201D, and on the ``" pair.

(b) Fix powerShellLine in ONE pass. Prefix one backtick to every backtick, $, ", U+201C, U+201D and U+201E, and leave every other character alone. A single pass cannot re-escape the backticks it adds. Chained replace calls would have to escape the backtick first, and escaping " first reopens PWNED2.

(c) Make bashWrapPowerShell's un-escape the exact inverse: drop each escaping backtick and keep the character after it. For example, use a regex for a backtick followed by any character, replaced by that character. Every backtick powerShellLine emits is an escape. The bash re-escape (\\, \", \$, \`) is unchanged, and bash needs nothing for curly quotes. Update the KDoc to say so.

Compatibility: the only escapes in the pinned lines are the backtick-$ before env, so PINNED_LEGACY, the accounts pins and AccountPresentationTest still match byte for byte. Do not edit them.

Error handling: no new failure path. Both functions stay total string transforms behind the unchanged control-character refusal.
